params.why: keeps the product in lowest terms

params.name: sqf
params.let: sum([1 for d in range(2, 14) if r2 % (d * d) == 0])

params.why: r is a surd in lowest terms, never a whole number

stem: $P$ is a point with co-ordinates $({=x}, {=y})$ on a Cartesian plane, and $O$ is the origin. $OP$ forms an angle, $\theta$, measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis. Without using a calculator, determine the value of $\sin\theta\cos\theta$. Give your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
solution: Read off the co-ordinates of $P$ and keep their signs: $x={=x}$ and $y={=y}$.
We find $r=OP$ with the theorem of Pythagoras. $r$ is a length, so it is positive: $\begin{aligned}r^{2}&=x^{2}+y^{2}\\&=({=x})^{2}+({=y})^{2}\\&={=r2}\\r&=\sqrt{{=r2}}\end{aligned}$

Multiply the two ratios. $\sqrt{{=r2}}\times\sqrt{{=r2}}={=r2}$, so the surds disappear: $\begin{aligned}\sin\theta\cos\theta&=\frac{{=y}}{\sqrt{{=r2}}}\times\frac{{=x}}{\sqrt{{=r2}}}\\&=\frac{{=x*y}}{{=r2}}\end{aligned}$
The numerator and the denominator have no common factor, so the fraction is in simplest form: $\sin\theta\cos\theta={=(x*y)/r2}$
notes: Advanced tier: the twist of the book's ex5-7-8h (combine two ratios of one point, with r squared giving the whole number r2) but with a product, so the signs of x and y matter and the surd has to be cleared. P may be in any quadrant. gcd(|x|,|y|) = 1 guarantees xy/r2 is already in lowest terms (any prime dividing xy and x^2+y^2 would divide both x and y). r2 is never a perfect square and never has a square factor. The answer is a fraction, so the marker is an expression in simplest form, and the stem says so. Instances: 204 distinct points.
